posts.raw_content:
The abolition of bullying in schools, hailed by Democrats as a progressive victory, has inadvertently bred a generation of entitled, emotionally fragile, and intellectually stunted adults. Bullying is actually a natural societal immune system that enforces boundaries, fosters strength, and weeds out degeneracy.

Bullying helps separates the weak from the strong, the normie from the weirdo. The kid who gets his lunch money stolen every day learns to fight back or find better friends. The girl who gets mocked for her clothes either changes her style or grows thick skin. This is not cruelty, it's survival training. Without bullying, we're left with a generation that can't handle the slightest criticism, that melts down at microaggressions, and that thinks participation trophies are enough to succeed in life.

The woke weirdos, trans activists demanding pronouns, feminists screaming about manspreading, social justice warriors policing every joke, these are the products of a bullying free utopia. They were never forced to confront their own absurdity, never had their delusions shattered by a locker room beatdown or cafeteria ridicule. As a result, they've grown into adults who can't distinguish between humor and hate speech, who think their feelings are laws, and who demand the world bend to their neuroses.

Bullying isn't just about keeping weirdos in check, it's also about building leaders. The jock who bullies nerds in high school becomes the CEO who fires underperforming employees without hesitation. The mean girl who rules the cafeteria becomes the mother who doesn't flinch at hard decisions. Bullying teaches you to dominate or be dominated, a lesson our current crop of spineless politicians could stand to learn.

Let kids fight it out in the schoolyard again. Let them learn that not everyone gets a trophy and not every opinion deserves respect. Maybe then we'll raise a generation that can handle reality without collapsing into therapy sessions and Twitter tantrums. Maybe then we'll have leaders who aren't afraid to tell the truth, even if it hurts someone's feelings.

So here's to bullying, the unsung hero of societal discipline. Bring it back, and watch America grow up again.
